---
title: "PPMI Molecular Cluster Creation with UPDRS-based Features"
author: "Andrew Gumbert"
date: "September 2025 - August 2026"
output: html_document
---

Description:

This file performs clustering analysis with the selected multi-omics features from PPMI_Data_Exploration_Transcriptomics_based_on_UPDRS.Rmd and PPMI_Data_Exploration_Proteomics_based_on_UPDRS.Rmd. The file considers the full cohort of sporadic cases, even those that did not have sufficient UPDRS data to qualify for a UPDRS-based cluster assignment. Accordingly, this program loads and processes the omics data directly from the raw files to capture all sporadic cases. With the clustering results, this file tests the clusters for clinical implications and differences with respect to covariates.


### Sets up global variables and the main curated data set

```{r}
main_directory <- "/Users/Andrew/Desktop/PPMI_Data_Files"
```

```{r}
# sets global variable for the color scheme of the clusters
cluster_colors = c("brown", "orange", "cornflowerblue")
```


```{r}
# Sets boolean that will determine whether the analyses consider CSF proteomic data.
# CSF data originates from a more invasive procedure (lumbar puncture) relative to
# data from urine and whole blood. Therefore, setting this variable to FALSE will
# only consider data from the minimally invasive tests without the reliance on the 
# invasive lumbar puncture procedure. 
consider_CSF_data <- TRUE
```


```{r}
# Reads in the curated data set containing LEDD information
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7049272/importing-excel-files-into-r-xlsx-or-xls
# for help with this code
curated_data <- read_excel(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_Curated_Data_Cut_Public_20251112.xlsx"), sheet = 1)
```

```{r}
# filters to the full sporadic PD cohort
curated_data_full_sporadic_cohort <- curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(subgroup == "Sporadic PD" & EVENT_ID == "BL") 
full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs <- curated_data_full_sporadic_cohort$PATNO
length(full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs)
```

### The following code blocks extract and process the transcriptomic data associated with the full sporadic cohort

```{r}

# Takes in the metadata files for RNAseq and sample metadata
# This file is from https://ida.loni.usc.edu/pages/access/geneticData.jsp
RNAseq_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/metaDataIR3.csv"))
# This file is from https://ida.loni.usc.edu/web/ppmi-rnaseq-app#Accessdata
sample_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "meta_data.11192021.csv"))

# Checks dimensions and the number of unique samples in the metadata (should be the same)
dim(RNAseq_metadata)
length(unique(RNAseq_metadata$HudAlphaID))
dim(sample_metadata)
length(unique(sample_metadata$HudAlphaSampleName))

# joins the two metadata files and removes old files
RNAseq_metadata <- dplyr::rename(RNAseq_metadata, HudAlphaSampleName = "HudAlphaID")
joined_metadata <- inner_join(RNAseq_metadata, sample_metadata, by = "HudAlphaSampleName")
rm(RNAseq_metadata, sample_metadata)

# checks the dimensions of joined metadata compared to unique samples (should be the same)
dim(joined_metadata)
length(unique(joined_metadata$HudAlphaSampleName))

# stores the metadata filtered to only include samples that passed quality control
quality_metadata <- joined_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(QCflagIR3 == "pass")

dim(quality_metadata)

# joins genomic data to the RNAseq data in case downstream analyses consider the genomic data
genetic_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "iu_genetic_consensus_20250515_18Jul2025.csv"))
genetic_metadata <- genetic_metadata %>% dplyr::rename("PATNO.x" = PATNO )
overall_RNAseq_metadata <- left_join(quality_metadata, genetic_metadata, by = "PATNO.x")

dim(overall_RNAseq_metadata)
```

```{r}
# filters to only PATNOs with RNA seq QC metrics meeting the threshold
quality_RNA_full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs <- (overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO.x %in% full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs & CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL" & RIN.Value.x >= 7 & multimapped_percent + uniquely_mapped_percent >= 80) %>% dplyr::arrange(PATNO.x))$PATNO.x
```


```{r}
# Gets just the relevant filtered sample IDs from baseline to use in setting up the counts matrix
filtered_sample_ids_bl_full_sporadic_cohort <- sapply(sort(quality_RNA_full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs), function(patient_id) {(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO.x == patient_id & Month == "M0"))$HudAlphaSampleName})

# Gets the label names for each gene from the first gene quanitification file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42819131/read-tab-delimited-text-file
# for help with processing tab deliminations 
gene_names <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/PPMI-Phase1-IR3.1009.POOL.0003202425.5104-SL-0095.longRNA-NEBKAP.salmon.genes.sf"), sep = "\t", header=T)$Name

# creates data frame to store the expression matrix
PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort <- data.frame(gene_names)

# counter to help track progress of loop (see below)
counter = 0

# Fills the expression matrix with the data from each genomic file
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14958516/read-all-files-in-directory-and-apply-multiple-functions-to-each-data-frame
# for help with accessing all files in a directory
# Credit to https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/stringr/vignettes/regular-expressions.html
# for help with regular expressions
# Credit to https://www.dataquest.io/blog/add-column-to-dataframe-in-r/
# for help with manipulating data frames
# Credit to https://www.w3schools.com/r/r_for_loop.asp
# for help with setting up the for loop
gene_files <- list.files(path = file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant"), pattern = "*.genes.sf")
for (x in gene_files){
    # determines if the file corresponds to filtered PD samples
    if(str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....") %in% filtered_sample_ids_bl_full_sporadic_cohort){
      
        # adds the data from the file to the expression matrix.
        PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort[str_extract(x, "5104-SL-....")] <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "PPMI_RNAseq_IR3_Analysis/quant/", x), sep = "\t", header=T)$NumReads
        
        # keeps track of counter and prints at every 100 counts
        counter <- counter + 1
        if (counter %% 100 == 0){
            print(counter)
        }
    }
}

# puts gene names as the row names
PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort <- column_to_rownames(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort, "gene_names")

# sets the column names to be patient ids rather than sample ids
colnames(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort) <- sapply(colnames(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort), function(sample_id){(overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(HudAlphaSampleName == sample_id))$PATNO.x})

# orders the columns by ascending patient id
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29873293/dplyr-order-columns-alphabetically-in-r
# for help with this step
PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort <- dplyr::select(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort, order(colnames(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort))) 
```

```{r}
# loads the selected transcriptomic features from "PPMI_Data_Exploration_Transcriptomics_based_on_UPDRS.Rmd"
selected_tran_features <- read.table(file.path(main_directory, "selected_transcriptomic_features_from_UPDRS_A_vs_B.txt"))$V1
```



```{r}
# filters data to selected transcriptomics features from PPMI_Data_Exploration_Transcriptomics_based_on_UPDRS.Rmd and prepares for vst
PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort_before_vst <- PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort %>% dplyr::filter(row.names(.) %in% selected_tran_features) %>% arrange(row.names(.))

# checks the dimensions and head of the data frame
dim(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort_before_vst)
head(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort_before_vst)
```


```{r}
# Uses a variance stabilizing transformation on the RNA seq data.
# Credit to https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
# and https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/DESeq2/versions/1.12.3/topics/vst
# and https://rpubs.com/shilpayadahalli/1018298
# for help with this code.
transcriptomic_data_DES_obj_full_sporadic_cohort_for_vst <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = round(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort_before_vst),
                                                                            colData = (data.frame(patno = colnames(PD_expression_counts_bl_full_sporadic_cohort_before_vst)) %>% column_to_rownames("patno")), 
                                                                            design = ~ 1)
                                                                      
vst_transcriptomic_data_full_sporadic_cohort <- varianceStabilizingTransformation(transcriptomic_data_DES_obj_full_sporadic_cohort_for_vst)

# extracts the processed transcriptomic exp data meeting the threshold to use in downstream analyses
transcriptomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_full_sporadic_cohort <- t(as.data.frame(assay(vst_transcriptomic_data_full_sporadic_cohort)))
```

```{r}
# prints the dimensions of the processed transcriptomic data frame
dim(transcriptomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_full_sporadic_cohort)
```


```{r}
# scales the processed transcriptomic exp data to use in clustering
transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort <- scale(transcriptomic_exp_data_meeting_threshold_full_sporadic_cohort)
```



```{r}
# checks processed data for normality
hist(as.data.frame(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)[[1]])
hist(as.data.frame(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)[[2]])
hist(as.data.frame(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)[[3]])
hist(as.data.frame(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)[[4]])
hist(as.data.frame(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)[[5]])
```

#### The following code blocks create a summary table with the numbers of participants and their demographic information across the different omics modalities


```{r}

# defines function to return the mean age and standard deviation of a participant group
get_mean_age_and_sd_as_string <- function(participant_group){
  
    paste0(round(mean((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$age)), " (" , round(sd((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$age)), ")")
}

# defines function to return the median disease duration and IQR of a participant group
get_median_duration_and_IQR_as_string <- function(participant_group){

    paste0(round(median((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$duration_yrs, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1), " [" , round(quantile((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$duration_yrs, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1), " - ", round(quantile((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$duration_yrs, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1), "]")
}

# defines function to return the male percentage of a participant group
get_male_percent <- function(participant_group){
    round(100 * mean((curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% participant_group & EVENT_ID == "BL"))$SEX == 1))
}
```

```{r}
# defines a function to create a row in the demographic summary table
# "name" determines the name of the row as a string
# "participant_group" is the list of PATNOs in the group as a vector
create_summary_table_row <- function(name, participant_group){
  
    # returns the row with the number of participants, the mean age, the median disease duration, and the percentage of males.
    return(data.frame(group = c(name),
                      Num_participants = length(participant_group),
                      #With_UPDRS_clust = sum(participant_group%in%c(cluster_A_patients_overall,cluster_B_patients_overall)),
                      Mean_age = get_mean_age_and_sd_as_string(participant_group),
                      Median_disease_duration = get_median_duration_and_IQR_as_string(participant_group),
                      Male_percent = get_male_percent(participant_group)) %>% column_to_rownames("group"))
}
```



```{r}
# creates the first part of the table with to total cases, cases with tran data, and cases with urine prot data
omics_sample_summary_table <- rbind(create_summary_table_row("Total cases available",
                                                             full_sporadic_cohort_PATNOs),
                                    create_summary_table_row("Cases with transcriptomic data",
                                                             row.names(transcriptomic_exp_for_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)),
                                    create_summary_table_row("Cases with urine proteomic data",
                                                             row.names(proteomic_exp_for_clustering_urine_full_sporadic_cohort)))

# if considering CSF data, adds a column for the CSF sample and then adds the final column for participants with all data types
if(consider_CSF_data){
  
    omics_sample_summary_table <- rbind(omics_sample_summary_table,
                                        create_summary_table_row("Cases with CSF prot data",
                                                             row.names(proteomic_exp_for_clustering_CSF_full_sporadic_cohort)),
                                        create_summary_table_row("Cases with tran, urine prot, and CSF prot data",
                                                             cases_with_selected_omics_data))
    
# if not considering CSF data, adds the final column for participants who have both tran and urine prot data
} else {
  
    omics_sample_summary_table <- rbind(omics_sample_summary_table,
                                        create_summary_table_row("Cases with both tran and urine prot data",
                                                                 cases_with_selected_omics_data))
}

# displays the summary table
omics_sample_summary_table
```



### Runs iClusterBayes to generate multi-omic clusters from the transcriptomic and proteomic data

```{r}

# initializes the variable to store the results of iClusterBayes
icluster_tune_results_full_sporadic_cohort <- c()

if(consider_CSF_data){
   
    # sets seed to produce consistent iCluster results
    set.seed(648)

    # uses tune.iClusterBayes to find ideal number of clusters
    # credit to https://rdrr.io/bioc/iClusterPlus/man/tune.iClusterBayes.html
    # for help with this function
    # Credit to https://rdrr.io/bioc/iClusterPlus/man/iClusterBayes.html
    # for help with the iClusterBayes function.
    icluster_tune_results_full_sporadic_cohort <- tune.iClusterBayes(dt1 = transcriptomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt2 = urine_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt3 = CSF_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, type = c("gaussian", "gaussian", "gaussian"))
  
} else {

    # sets seed to produce consistent iCluster results
    set.seed(648)

    # uses tune.iClusterBayes to find ideal number of clusters
    icluster_tune_results_full_sporadic_cohort <- tune.iClusterBayes(dt1 = transcriptomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt2 = urine_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, type = c("gaussian", "gaussian"))
    
}

sapply(1:6, function(i){icluster_tune_results_full_sporadic_cohort$fit[[i]]$BIC})
```

```{r}
# gets the iClusterBayes results from the optimal tuning in the code chunk above
```

```{r}
# defines function to return median values in the curated metadata from years 0 - 3
# from a specified participant id and score type
get_med_Y0_3_Scores <- function(patno, score_type){
    return(median(unlist(sapply(c(0:3), function(years){(curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == patno & YEAR == years))[[score_type]]})), na.rm = TRUE))
}
```



```{r}
# sets a type of UPDRS score to test. Can be either "updrs_totscore", "updrs1_score", "updrs2_score", "updrs3_score", or "updrs4_score".
PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test <- "updrs_totscore"


# For each cluster, extracts the median UPDRS scores from each patient across years 0 - 3
clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort <- unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data[icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 1], function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test)}))

clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort <- unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data[icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 2], function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test)}))

clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort <- unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data[icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 3], function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test)}))

# create ggplot boxplot to show score distribution differences by cluster
# Credit to https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-colors-how-to-change-colors-automatically-and-manually
# for help with setting up custom colors.
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/35618260/remove-legend-ggplot-2-2
# for help with removing the legend.
ggplot_updrs_scores_by_clust <-  ggplot(data.frame(scores = c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), clust = c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("3", length(clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)))), aes(x = clust, y = scores, fill = clust)) + scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colors) + theme(legend.position = "none")

# prints the ggplot with a legend based on the relevant UPDRS section, as a box plot
ggplot_updrs_scores_by_clust + labs(x = "Cluster", y = paste0("Median ", PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test, " from Years 0 - 3")) + geom_boxplot()

# prints the ggplot with a legend based on the relevant UPDRS section, as a jitter plot over a boxplot with reduced transparency
# credit to https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_boxplot.html
# and https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_jitter.html
# for help with this code
ggplot_updrs_scores_by_clust + labs(x = "Cluster", y = paste0("Median ", PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test, " from Years 0 - 3")) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + theme_bw()

# creates an additional set of plots with a cleaner y-axis label if using the total score.
if(PPMI_molecular_clusters_score_to_test == "updrs_totscore"){
    # the box plot
    print(ggplot_updrs_scores_by_clust + labs(x = "Cluster", y = paste0("Median UPDRS Total Scores from Years 0 - 3")) + geom_boxplot())
  
    # the jitter plot over the box plot
    print(ggplot_updrs_scores_by_clust + labs(x = "Cluster", y = paste0("Median UPDRS Total Scores from Years 0 - 3")) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + theme_bw())
}

# performs kruskal test to get significance of score differences across clusters.
kruskal.test(scores ~ clust, data.frame(scores = c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), clust = c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("3", length(clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)))))
```

```{r}
# stores the clustering results with covariates to test for robustness of clinical implications
clustering_results_with_covariates <- icluster_metadata_full_sporadic_cohort %>% mutate(UPDRS_outcome = unlist(sapply(PATNO, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs_totscore")})), MoCA_outcome = unlist(sapply(PATNO, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "moca")})), UPSIT_outcome = unlist(sapply(PATNO, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "upsit")})), age = unlist(sapply(PATNO, function(patno){(curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == 0 & PATNO == patno))[["age"]]})), sex = as.factor(unlist(sapply(PATNO, function(patno){(curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == 0 & PATNO == patno))[["SEX"]]}))))

# performs statistical tests on the robustness of clinical implications after adjusting for covariates

# tests UPDRS outcomes
kruskal.test(UPDRS_outcome ~ as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates)

# tests MoCA outcomes
kruskal.test(MoCA_outcome ~ as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates)
summary(aov(MoCA_outcome ~ as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates))
summary(aov(MoCA_outcome ~ age + sex + as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates))

# tests UPSIT outcomes
kruskal.test(UPSIT_outcome ~ as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates)
summary(aov(UPSIT_outcome ~ as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates))
summary(aov(UPSIT_outcome ~ age + sex + as.factor(iclust), clustering_results_with_covariates))
```

```{r}
# gets data frame with UPDRS scores and latent dimensions
UPDRS_scores_by_latent_dims <- data.frame(latent_dim_1 = icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$meanZ[,1], latent_dim_2 = icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$meanZ[,2], UPDRS_totscores = sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs_totscore")}))

# plots the UPDRS total scores by the latent dimensions
```

```{r}
# This code block tests for relationships between another variable and the iClusterBayes latent space dimensions

test_var_across_latent_dims <- function(var_of_interest){

    # gets data frame with the variable of interest and latent dimensions
    var_by_latent_dims <- data.frame(latent_dim_1 = icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$meanZ[,1], latent_dim_2 = icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$meanZ[,2], var_of_interest_values = sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){(curated_data %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == 0 & PATNO == patno))[[var_of_interest]]}))
    
    # plots the variable of interest by the latent dimensions
    # credit to https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_smooth.html
    # for help with this code
    print(ggplot(var_by_latent_dims, aes(x = latent_dim_1, y = var_of_interest_values)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) + labs(x = "1st Latent Dimension from iClusterBayes meanZ output", y = paste0(var_of_interest, " (at baseline)")) + theme_bw())
    print(ggplot(var_by_latent_dims, aes(x = latent_dim_2, y = var_of_interest_values)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) + labs(x = "2nd Latent Dimension from iClusterBayes meanZ output", y = paste0(var_of_interest, " (at baseline)")) + theme_bw())

    # gets summaries of linear models of the relationship between the variable of interest and latent dimensions
    print(summary(lm(var_of_interest_values ~ latent_dim_1, var_by_latent_dims)))
    print(summary(lm(var_of_interest_values ~ latent_dim_2, var_by_latent_dims)))
}
```

### The following code blocks perform pairwise and effect size tests on the scores by cluster

```{r}
# performs pairwise tests on the UPDRS scores across the clusters created above (PPMI sporadic)
pairwise.wilcox.test(c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("3", length(clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort))))

# repeats test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment
pairwise.wilcox.test(c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("3", length(clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort))), p.adjust.method = "BH")
```

```{r}
# finds the effect size for the difference in scores between the first two clusters
# credit to https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/rstatix/versions/0.7.3/topics/wilcox_effsize
# for help with this function
wilcox_effsize(data.frame(score = c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), clust = c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)))), score ~ clust)

# finds the effect size for the difference in scores between the first cluster and the other two clusters (group 1 vs group 2)
wilcox_effsize(data.frame(score = c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), group = c(rep("1", length(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort)), rep("2", length(c(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort))))), score ~ group)

# tests significance of difference between cluster 1 and the other two clusters combined
wilcox.test(c(clust1_scores_full_sporadic_cohort), c(clust2_scores_full_sporadic_cohort, clust3_scores_full_sporadic_cohort))

```

```{r}
# gets the overview of genetic information from PPMI
```

```{r}
# build data frame to store overview of genetic information from sporadic clustering cases
genetic_info_of_cases_sporadic_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort <- data.frame(PATNO = cases_with_selected_omics_data)

# initializes variables to store genetic group and polygenic risk score
ancestry_group <- c()
polygenic_risk_score <- c()

# fills in the data frame with genetic group and polygenic risk score information
for (case in cases_with_selected_omics_data){
  
    # gets genetic group data 
    # if no value in the genetic data then record an "NA"
    if(length((genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_InfPop) == 0){
         ancestry_group <- c(ancestry_group, NA)
    # if there is one value then record that value
    }else if(length((genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_InfPop) == 1){
         ancestry_group <- c(ancestry_group, (genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_InfPop)
    # if there are more than one value for a case, then record a duplicate measurement
    }else{
        ancestry_group <- c(ancestry_group, "Duplicate value")
    }
  
    # gets polygenic risk score data 
    # if no value in the genetic data then record an "NA"
    if(length((genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_PRSp90) == 0){
         polygenic_risk_score <- c(polygenic_risk_score, NA)
    # if there is one value then record that value
    }else if(length((genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_PRSp90) == 1){
         polygenic_risk_score <- c(polygenic_risk_score, (genetic_overview_information %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO == case))$Genetic_PRS_PRSp90)
    # if there are more than one value for a case, then record a duplicate measurement
    }else{
        polygenic_risk_score <- c(polygenic_risk_score, "Duplicate value")
    }
}

# store the measurements in the data frame and print the head
genetic_info_of_cases_sporadic_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort$ancestry_group <- ancestry_group
genetic_info_of_cases_sporadic_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort$PRS <- polygenic_risk_score
head(genetic_info_of_cases_sporadic_clustering_full_sporadic_cohort)
```

### The following code blocks perform repeated tests to account for randomness over many iterations, using multi-omics data



```{r}

# runs an iteration of iclusterbayes and extracts kruskal p-value applied to median UPDRS scores from years 0-3 across clusters
iterate_icluster_and_apply_kruskal_test_full_sporadic_cohort <- function(num_clusts){

    # prints the number of clusters to keep track of progress
    print(num_clusts)
  
    # initializes iteration results variable
    iteration_results <- c()
    
    #iteration_results <- iClusterBayes(dt1 = proteomic_exp_for_clustering_CSF_full_sporadic_cohort, type = c("gaussian"), K = num_clusts - 1)
  
    # gets the iClusterBayes iteration results with or without considering CSF data
    if(consider_CSF_data){
        iteration_results <- iClusterBayes(dt1 = transcriptomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt2 = urine_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt3 = CSF_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, type = c("gaussian", "gaussian", "gaussian"), K = num_clusts - 1)
      
    } else {
        iteration_results <- iClusterBayes(dt1 = transcriptomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, dt2 = urine_proteomics_for_icluster_full_sporadic_cohort, type = c("gaussian", "gaussian"), K = num_clusts - 1)
    
    }

    # gets the median year 0 - 3 UPDRS section and total scores from each cluster
    iteration_scores_and_clust <- data.frame(sec1_score = unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs1_score")})),
                                             sec2_score = unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs2_score")})),
                                             sec3_score = unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs3_score")})),
                                             sec4_score = unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs4_score")})),
                                             tot_score = unlist(sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "updrs_totscore")})),
                                             clust = iteration_results$clusters)

    # performs kruskal test to get significance of score differences across clusters.
    return(sapply(c("sec1_score", "sec2_score", "sec3_score", "sec4_score", "tot_score"), function(section){((kruskal.test(as.formula(paste0(section, " ~ clust")), iteration_scores_and_clust))$p.value)}))

}

iteration_num_clusts <- c(rep(2, 10), rep(3, 10), rep(4, 10), rep(5, 10))

iteration_kruskal_results_full_sporadic_cohort <- sapply(iteration_num_clusts, function(num_clusts){iterate_icluster_and_apply_kruskal_test_full_sporadic_cohort(num_clusts)})
```

```{r}

# visualizes the results of multiple iterations as boxplots
# credit to https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-add-straight-lines-to-a-plot-horizontal-vertical-and-regression-lines
# for help with this code
sapply(c("sec1_score", "sec2_score", "sec3_score", "sec4_score", "tot_score"), 
       function(section){
         print(ggplot(data.frame(kruskal_pvals = iteration_kruskal_results_full_sporadic_cohort[section,], num_clusts = iteration_num_clusts), aes(x = as.factor(num_clusts), y = kruskal_pvals)) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, fill = "grey") + geom_jitter(width = 0.1) + labs(x = "Number of Clusters", y = "Kruskal Test P-Value Results", title = paste0( "Distribution of Kruskal Test P-Value Results (Med Y0-3 ", section, ")")) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, color = "red") + theme_bw())
         
         # prints the median values for each section and number of clusters
         # credit to https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Round.html
         # for help with rounding
         for(n in unique(iteration_num_clusts)){
            print(paste0(section, " (", n, "): ", signif(median(iteration_kruskal_results_full_sporadic_cohort[section, iteration_num_clusts == n]), 2)))
         }
         }
       )
```


```{r}
# creates same graph as above but uses the negative logarithm of the p-values
sapply(c("sec1_score", "sec2_score", "sec3_score", "sec4_score", "tot_score"), 
       function(section){
         ggplot(data.frame(kruskal_pvals = iteration_kruskal_results_full_sporadic_cohort[section,], num_clusts = iteration_num_clusts), aes(x = as.factor(num_clusts), y = -log10(kruskal_pvals))) + geom_boxplot() + labs(x = "Number of Clusters", y = "-log10 of Kruskal Test P-Value Results", title = paste0("Distribution of Kruskal Test P-Value Results (CP Only, Med Y0-3 ", section, ")")) + geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), color = "red")
         }
```

```{r}
# this code block creates boxplots and performs kruskal tests to test for differences in moca scores by cluster.
```

```{r}
med_moca_scores_df <- data.frame(PATNO = cases_with_selected_omics_data, 
                                 med_moca_scores = sapply(cases_with_selected_omics_data, function(patno){get_med_Y0_3_Scores(patno, "moca")}), 
                                 clust = as.factor(icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters))

# check for no missing moca scores
all(!is.na(med_moca_scores_df$med_moca_scores))

# create ggplot boxplot to show moca distribution differences by cluster
# Credit to https://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-colors-how-to-change-colors-automatically-and-manually
# for help with setting up custom colors.
# Credit to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/35618260/remove-legend-ggplot-2-2
# for help with removing the legend.
ggplot(med_moca_scores_df, aes(x = clust, y = med_moca_scores, fill = clust)) + scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colors) + geom_boxplot() + labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Median MoCA Scores from Years 0 - 3") + theme(legend.position = "none")

# plots the MoCA scores by cluster as a jitter plot over a transparent box plot
# credit to https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_boxplot.html
# and https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_jitter.html
# for help with this code
ggplot(med_moca_scores_df, aes(x = clust, y = med_moca_scores, fill = clust)) + scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colors) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Median MoCA Scores from Years 0 - 3") + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme_bw()

table(med_moca_scores_df$clust)

# performs kruskal test to get significance of moca differences across clusters.
kruskal.test(med_moca_scores ~ clust, med_moca_scores_df)

# gets the Wilcoxon p-value and effect size of cluster 1 vs clusters 2 and 3 combined
med_moca_scores_df$clust_grouping <- case_when(med_moca_scores_df$clust %in% c(1) ~ 1,
                                               med_moca_scores_df$clust %in% c(2, 3) ~ 2)
wilcox.test(med_moca_scores ~ clust_grouping, med_moca_scores_df)
wilcox_effsize(med_moca_scores_df, med_moca_scores ~ clust_grouping)
```

```{r}
SAA_results <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "SAA_Biospecimen_Analysis_Results_21Feb2025.csv"))
dim(SAA_results)

SAA_results <- SAA_results %>% dplyr::filter(CLINICAL_EVENT == "BL" & PATNO %in% cases_with_selected_omics_data & SAAMethod == "Amprion-Alpha-synuclein-SAA" & SAA_Status != "Inconclusive") %>% arrange(PATNO)
```


```{r}
# checks for number of results and that there is one result per participant 
dim(SAA_results)
length(unique(SAA_results$PATNO))
```



```{r}
# calculates the mean values for the TTT_150h, T50_150h and AUC_150h.
# credit to https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/rowwise.html
# for helping with the rowwise and ungroup functions
SAA_results <- SAA_results %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(mean_TTT_150h = mean(c(TTT_150h_Rep1, TTT_150h_Rep2, TTT_150h_Rep3), na.rm = T)) %>% ungroup()
SAA_results <- SAA_results %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(mean_T50_150h = mean(c(T50_150h_Rep1, T50_150h_Rep2, T50_150h_Rep3), na.rm = T)) %>% ungroup()
SAA_results <- SAA_results %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(mean_AUC_150h = mean(c(AUC_150h_Rep1, AUC_150h_Rep2, AUC_150h_Rep3), na.rm = T)) %>% ungroup()
```



```{r}
# finds the clusters corresponding to the SAA data 
SAA_results <- SAA_results %>% mutate(clust = 
                                        case_when(PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 1]
                                                      ~ 1,
                                                  PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 2]
                                                      ~ 2,
                                                  PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 3]
                                                      ~ 3))
SAA_results$clust <- as.factor(SAA_results$clust)

table(SAA_results$clust)
```


```{r}
# this code block tests for differences in SAA status (positive/negative) by cluster
# credit to https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/chi-square-test-r
# for help with this code

# creates a contingency table with the SAA clusters and positive/negative status
SAA_contingency_table <- table(SAA_results$clust, SAA_results$SAA_Status)
print(SAA_contingency_table)

# performs the Chi-Squared test
chisq.test(SAA_contingency_table)
```




```{r}

# gets the number of participants with available mean TTT values by cluster
table((SAA_results %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(mean_TTT_150h)))$clust)

# visualizes and tests for differences in mean TTT 150h by clust

ggplot(SAA_results, aes(x = clust, y = mean_TTT_150h, fill = clust)) + scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colors) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Mean TTT (Hours)") + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme_bw()

# performs kruskal test to get significance of mean TTT 150h differences across clusters.
kruskal.test(mean_TTT_150h ~ clust, SAA_results)
```

#### The following code tests for differences in DaTscan measurements by cluster


```{r}

# loads the DaTscan data and filters to relevant participants and screening visits
DaTscan_df <- read.csv(file.path(main_directory, "DaTScan_Analysis_05Jan2024.csv"))
DaTscan_df <- DaTscan_df %>% dplyr::filter(PATNO %in% cases_with_selected_omics_data & EVENT_ID %in% c("SC")) %>% dplyr::arrange("PATNO")

# ensures all DaTscans were analyzed and have the same protocol 
table(DaTscan_df$DATSCAN_ANALYZED)
table(DaTscan_df$PROTOCOL)

# checks to ensure there are no duplicate scans for individual participants
length(DaTscan_df$PATNO)
length(unique(DaTscan_df$PATNO))

# assigns the cluster variable to each DaTscan result
DaTscan_df <- DaTscan_df %>% mutate(clust = 
                                        case_when(PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 1]
                                                      ~ 1,
                                                  PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 2]
                                                      ~ 2,
                                                  PATNO %in%
                                                     cases_with_selected_omics_data[
                                                     icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort$clusters == 3]
                                                      ~ 3))
DaTscan_df$clust <- as.factor(DaTscan_df$clust)

# shows the numbers of available scans per cluster
table(DaTscan_df$clust)
```

```{r}
# defines a function to create a plot and run a Kruskal-Wallis test on DaTscan data
# the function takes a brain region of interest as input
# creates a plot and performs the statistical test for the given brain region
analyze_DaTscan_SBR_from_brain_region <- function(brain_region){
  
    # prints the brain region for reference
    print(brain_region)

    # generates the box plot and jitter plot for SBR data by cluster in the given brain region
    print(ggplot(DaTscan_df, aes(x = clust, y = get(brain_region), fill = clust)) + scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_colors) + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) + geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + labs(title = brain_region, x = "Cluster", y = "SBR") + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 4, by = 1)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_text(size = 24), axis.title = element_text(size = 24), aspect.ratio = 1)) 

    # prints the results of a Kruskal-Wallis test for the SBR values by cluster
    print(kruskal.test(get(brain_region) ~ clust, DaTscan_df))
}

# runs the analysis from the function above for the left and right caudate and putamen
analyze_DaTscan_SBR_from_brain_region("DATSCAN_CAUDATE_R")
analyze_DaTscan_SBR_from_brain_region("DATSCAN_CAUDATE_L")
analyze_DaTscan_SBR_from_brain_region("DATSCAN_PUTAMEN_R")
analyze_DaTscan_SBR_from_brain_region("DATSCAN_PUTAMEN_L")

```




#### The following code blocks test for differences in UPDRS scores by cluster and potential covariates using linear mixed-effects modeling.



```{r}

# sets the clustering information to come from the main analysis based on the multi-omics data
LME_cluster_metadata = icluster_metadata_full_sporadic_cohort
LME_cluster_results = icluster_results_full_sporadic_cohort
```


```{r}
# sets up the RNA seq metadata to be able to use the relevant variables in the LME analysis
RNAseq_metadata_for_LME <- overall_RNAseq_metadata %>% mutate(YEAR = case_when(Month == "M0" ~ 0, Month == "M12" ~ 1, Month == "M24" ~ 2, Month == "M36" ~ 3), PATNO.x = as.character(PATNO.x), mapping_rate_percent = multimapped_percent + uniquely_mapped_percent) %>% dplyr::select(PATNO.x, YEAR, RIN.Value.x, mapping_rate_percent) %>% dplyr::rename(PATNO = "PATNO.x")

# gets RNA seq metadata for only baseline samples
RNAseq_metadata_for_LME_BL_only <- RNAseq_metadata_for_LME %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == 0) %>% dplyr::select(-c(YEAR))
```


```{r}
# extracts potential covariates and updrs data to use in the linear mixed-effects models
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model <- curated_data %>% dplyr::select(PATNO, SITE, updrs1_score, updrs2_score, updrs3_score, updrs4_score, updrs_totscore, YEAR, age_at_visit, SEX, agediag, LEDD) %>% mutate(taking_medication = LEDD > 0, disease_duration = age_at_visit - agediag)

# finds the cluster assignment of each participant in the data
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model <- updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% mutate(clust = 
                                                         case_when(PATNO %in%
                                                                   LME_cluster_metadata$PATNO[
                                                                   LME_cluster_results$clusters == 1]
                                                                    ~ 1,
                                                                   PATNO %in%
                                                                   LME_cluster_metadata$PATNO[
                                                                   LME_cluster_results$clusters == 2]
                                                                    ~ 2,
                                                                   PATNO %in%
                                                                   LME_cluster_metadata$PATNO[
                                                                   LME_cluster_results$clusters == 3]
                                                                    ~ 3,
                                                                   TRUE ~ 0)) # cluster 0 is given to label results that are not clustered

# prints the total number of items by cluster
table(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model$clust)

# filters to years 0 - 3 after baseline with a cluster assignment
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model <- updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% dplyr::filter(clust != 0 & YEAR %in% c(0, 1, 2, 3))

# checks the dimensions of the data
dim(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model)

# adds polygenic risk score and genetic PCs to the data for LME analysis
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model <- updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% left_join(dplyr::select(genetic_overview_information, PATNO, Genetic_PRS_PRSp90, Genetic_PRS_PC1, Genetic_PRS_PC2, Genetic_PRS_PC3) %>% mutate(PATNO = as.character(PATNO)), by = "PATNO")

# adds relevant RNAseq metadata to the data frame for LME analysis

# with only baseline RNAseq data to reflect how clusters are derived from the baseline data
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data <- updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% left_join(RNAseq_metadata_for_LME_BL_only, by = "PATNO")

# with RNAseq metadata from each year for expanded analysis beyond the baseline
updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model <- updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% left_join(RNAseq_metadata_for_LME, by = c("PATNO", "YEAR"))

# checks the dimensions of the data again
dim(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model)


# prints the number of results by cluster
table(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model$clust)

# prints the number of results by cluster and year
table(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model$YEAR, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model$clust)
```


```{r}
# plots the UPDRS total score by cluster and year for each participant
ggplot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model, aes(x = YEAR, y = updrs_totscore, group = PATNO, color = as.factor(clust))) + geom_line() + labs(title = "UPDRS Total Score by Cluster and Year for Each Participant", color = "Cluster") + scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors)

# plots the UPDRS total score by cluster and age at visit for each participant
ggplot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model, aes(x = age_at_visit, y = updrs_totscore, group = PATNO, color = as.factor(clust))) + geom_line() + labs(title = "UPDRS Total Score by Cluster and Age at Visit for Each Participant", color = "Cluster") + scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors)

# plots the UPDRS total score by cluster and disease duration for each participant
ggplot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model, aes(x = disease_duration, y = updrs_totscore, group = PATNO, color = as.factor(clust))) + geom_line() + labs(title = "UPDRS Total Score by Cluster and Disease Duration at Visit for Each Participant", color = "Cluster") + scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors)
```

```{r}
# performs wilcox tests on the UPDRS scores by sex at year 0 across all clusters
```

```{r}
# finds the median UPDRS total score by cluster and year

# plots the median UPDRS total score by cluster and year
ggplot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_clust_medians, aes(x = YEAR, y = clust_median_updrs_totscore, group = as.factor(clust), color = as.factor(clust))) + geom_line(linewidth = 3) + labs(title = "Median UPDRS Total Score by Cluster and Year", color = "Cluster") + scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors)

# This code performs a chi-squared test on the numbers of participants taking and not taking medication each 
# year by cluster to determine if the differences are statistically significant.
# Year 0 is not included because there are too few participants taking medication to satisfy the assumptions of 
# the chi-squared test.
sapply(c(1:3), function(year){chisq.test(table((updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == year))$clust, (updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model %>% dplyr::filter(YEAR == year))$taking_medication))$p.value})
```

```{r}
# creates the linear mixed effects model
# uses only baseline RNA seq data because only baseline transcriptomic data contributed to clustering
updrs_totscore_lmer <- lmer(updrs_totscore ~ YEAR + age_at_visit + disease_duration + as.factor(taking_medication) + as.factor(SEX) + Genetic_PRS_PRSp90 + Genetic_PRS_PC1 + Genetic_PRS_PC2 + Genetic_PRS_PC3 + RIN.Value.x + mapping_rate_percent + as.factor(clust) + (1 + YEAR | PATNO), data = updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data)

# checks for approximate linear relationships between UPDRS total scores and covariates
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$YEAR, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$age_at_visit, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$disease_duration, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$Genetic_PRS_PRSp90, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$RIN.Value.x, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)
plot(updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$mapping_rate_percent, updrs_data_for_mixed_effects_model_with_only_BL_RNAseq_data$updrs_totscore)


# checks the normality of residuals assumption of linear mixed effects modeling
qqnorm(resid(updrs_totscore_lmer), main = "Normal Q-Q Plot - UPDRS Total Score Residuals")
hist(resid(updrs_totscore_lmer), main = "UPDRS Total Score Residuals")
```

```{r}
# prints key results of the linear mixed effects modeling
summary(updrs_totscore_lmer)
```
